intro.html: Secrets come in many shapes: a plan kept quiet, a glance no one is meant to see, a talent no one has discovered yet, a message no one can read. This topic gives each its own word.

Secret actions: covert, clandestine, surreptitious, furtive, stealthy. Hidden meanings and motives: cryptic, veiled, ulterior. Hidden things: latent (there but not yet showing), elusive (hard to catch).

Notice the shades. Covert and clandestine describe whole plans; surreptitious, furtive and stealthy describe how a person moves or looks; and furtive adds a guilty air, since it comes from the Latin word for thief.

words.def: secret; not openly shown or done
words.ex: Lila shot a {covert} glance at the clock, hoping the teacher would not notice.
words.ctx: The surprise party was a {covert} operation: invitations were passed in whispers, and the guest of honor never suspected a thing.
words.etym: From Old French covert, “covered,” from covrir (to cover).

mn.text: Behind the sofa, under a blanket, the cousins whisper their plans for Mom’s surprise party; the whole plan is kept under cover, {covert}.

scene.alt: Two children hide behind a sofa, whispering surprise-party plans while their mother reads, unaware.

words.def: done in secret, often because it is not allowed
words.ex: The twins held a {clandestine} midnight feast in the attic.
words.ctx: Because the old king had banned all music, the villagers held {clandestine} concerts in barns and cellars, with lookouts posted at every door.

mn.text: At midnight the cat clan meets on the rooftop by lantern light, so the dogs below never find out; their meeting is {clandestine}.

scene.alt: Three cats meet secretly by lantern light at night while a dog sleeps nearby.

words.def: done secretly so as not to be noticed
words.ex: Kai slipped a {surreptitious} carrot to the dog under the table.
words.ctx: During the long speech, Rosa took a {surreptitious} look at her phone, tilting it below the table so the speaker would not notice.
words.etym: From Latin surripere, “to snatch secretly”: sub- (under, secretly) + rapere (to seize).

mn.text: When Mom turns to the stove, Kai sneaks his carrots under the table to the dog; the quick, secret handoff is {surreptitious}.

scene.alt: A boy secretly passes a carrot to the dog under the table while his mother looks away.

words.def: sly and secret, as if trying not to get caught
words.ex: The raccoon cast a {furtive} look over its shoulder before diving into the trash can.
words.ctx: His {furtive} manner gave him away: he kept glancing at the door, hiding his hands in his pockets and jumping whenever anyone spoke.
words.etym: From Latin furtivus, “stolen, secret,” from fur (thief).

mn.cue: FUR = THIEF: a sly, guilty look
mn.text: The furry little thief tiptoes off with the fish, glancing back over its shoulder again and again; that sly, guilty look is {furtive}.

scene.alt: A cat sneaks away with a fish, glancing back guiltily, while the cook looks the other way.

words.def: moving quietly and carefully so as not to be noticed
words.ex: The {stealthy} cat crept up on the butterfly without rustling a single leaf.
words.ctx: Unlike his noisy brother, who stomped up the stairs, Jonah was {stealthy}, slipping out the back door so quietly that even the dog did not wake.
words.etym: From stealth, which comes from the same old English root as steal.

mn.cue: STEAL-THY: steal past without a sound
mn.text: Jonah tiptoes past the sleeping dog in his socks, carrying his shoes; he steals by so quietly that he is {stealthy}.

scene.alt: A teen tiptoes in his socks past a sleeping dog, carrying his shoes.

words.def: present but hidden, or not yet active
words.ex: Lin had a {latent} gift for singing that no one discovered until the school musical.
words.ctx: The seeds lay {latent} in the dry desert soil for years; then a single heavy rain woke them, and the sand burst into bloom.
words.etym: From Latin latens, “lying hidden,” from latere (to lie hidden).

mn.cue: LATE-nt: there all along, it shows up LATE
mn.text: Seeds sleep in the desert sand for years, then bloom late, after one rare rain; the flowers were {latent} there the whole time.

scene.alt: After a rare rain, flowers suddenly bloom from the desert sand while a girl cheers.

words.ex: Grandpa left a {cryptic} note on the fridge: “Look where the moon sleeps.”
words.ctx: The treasure map’s directions were {cryptic}; instead of plain steps, they gave riddles about crooked trees and a rock that “laughs at the sea.”
words.etym: From Late Latin crypticus, from Greek kryptikos, “hidden,” from kryptein (to hide). A crypt is a hidden room.

mn.cue: CRYPT = hidden: a note in CODE
mn.text: Pip finds a note that says only “ZEBRA AT NOON, UNDER THE SECOND MOON,” and no one can work out what it means; it is {cryptic}.

scene.alt: A boy and an old professor puzzle over a mysterious coded note.

words.def: partly hidden; hinted at but not said openly
words.ex: Her remark about his “interesting” shoes was a {veiled} criticism.
words.ctx: The coach never said outright that the team had played poorly, but his {veiled} comment about “players who think practice is optional” made everyone stare at the floor.
words.etym: From veil, a thin cloth that covers the face: you can almost see what is behind it.

mn.text: Nana Lou smiles and says, “What lively music, dear!” but her hands are over her ears; her complaint is there, behind a thin veil. It is {veiled}.

labels.text: VEILED: a hint behind a curtain

scene.alt: A grandmother covers her ears while politely calling her grandson’s loud guitar playing lively.

words.def: hard to find, catch or remember
words.ex: The {elusive} snow leopard is rarely caught on camera.
words.ctx: The answer stayed {elusive}: every time Maya thought she had remembered the word, it slipped away again like a fish between her fingers.
words.etym: From Latin eludere, “to escape by a trick”: e- (out) + ludere (to play).
words.note: Elusive (hard to catch) is not illusive (unreal, like an illusion).

mn.cue: e-LOOSE-ive: it gets LOOSE every time
mn.text: Every time Pip swings his net, the butterfly slips loose and flutters just out of reach; it is {elusive}.

scene.alt: A boy leaps with a net as a butterfly flutters just out of reach.

words.def: hidden beyond what is openly said, as a secret reason
words.ex: Was his offer to wash the dishes sincere, or did he have an {ulterior} motive?
words.ctx: Dev’s sudden offer to walk the neighbor’s dog had an {ulterior} purpose: the neighbor baked the best brownies on the block and always paid in brownies.
words.note: Ulterior almost always describes a motive or a purpose.

mn.cue: ul-TERIOR: the real reason is in the inTERIOR
mn.text: Kai offers to vacuum Grandpa’s car, but his real reason is hidden in the car’s interior: the coins under the seats. His motive is {ulterior}.

scene.alt: A boy offers to clean a car while secretly thinking about the coins under its seats.

after.html: Two pairs to keep straight: covert (secret) and overt (open) are opposites, and elusive (hard to catch) is not illusive (unreal, like an illusion).

items.q: True or false: a covert plan is carried out openly for all to see.
items.why: False. Covert means secret; overt means open.

items.q: The fox was too quick for the hunters’ cameras; it remained…
items.why: Hard to catch is elusive. Illusive means unreal, like an illusion.
Latin latere means to lie hidden: a latent talent is there, but not yet showing.

items.q: Which word comes from the Latin word for thief and suggests a guilty air?
items.why: Furtive comes from Latin fur, thief: a furtive look is sly and guilty.
